In addition, for patients with 50–99% stenosis, perioperative combination antiplatelet therapy (dual antiplatelet therapy) may be considered after imaging has definitively excluded intracranial hemorrhage.

## Interpretation

Non-ESVS interpretation (clinical reasoning beyond the retrieved guideline text):
While the guidelines clearly state the antiplatelet recommendations, they do not provide explicit advice on the perioperative management of direct oral anticoagulants such as apixaban in patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing urgent CEA. In clinical practice, management of apixaban typically involves determining the timing of the last dose and assessing renal function to establish an appropriate DOAC hold period that minimizes bleeding risk without unduly delaying surgery. The decision to escalate to dual antiplatelet therapy also depends on confirming that there is no intracranial hemorrhage.
